title: Mýtus o rozpůlených lidech, který Platón vložil do úst komediografa
content:
V Platónově dialogu Hostina ze 4. století př. n. l. pronáší básník Aristofanés vtipný a dojemný příběh o původu lásky.

Lidé prý bývali kulatí, měli čtyři ruce, čtyři nohy a dvě tváře. Byli silní a drzí, a proto je Zeus rozpůlil. Od té doby se každá polovina snaží najít tu druhou.

Mýtus vysvětluje, proč si lásku spojujeme s pocitem dokončení a vzájemného doplnění. Platón ho ale nepovažoval za konečnou odpověď.

V dalším proslovu Sókratés předává učení kněžky Diotimy: láska je touha po kráse a dobru, která vede od jednoho těla k poznání krásy samotné. Dialog tak staví vedle sebe dva pohledy, citový a rozumový.

Diagrams, arrows and illustrated principles remain welcome when their visual form is itself expressive and suited to the article. Judge the whole composition, not just the number of objects or steps. A simple explanatory contrast or interaction is welcome when understood at a glance. If explanation would require many separate objects, several steps or arrows tracing which part implies the next, choose one recognizable aspect instead. The text explains the science and story; the picture does not need to explain the mechanism, prove the claim or summarize the whole article. A standalone relevant object is enough. Examples: a moving ambulance for Doppler effect; a book with a prohibition sign for a banned novel; a pulsar with a simple beam, without Earth, waveform, magnetic field or observation equipment. Metadata is context, not a checklist of objects to draw. Omit secondary subjects and explanatory marks when the main motif already works. Choose between a simple accompanying subject and a simple explanatory relationship according to context. A compact comparison or a useful single arrow is fine; avoid multistep experiments, networks of implications and inventories of disconnected scientific components. A small supporting symbol is welcome when immediately readable. Broad clean silhouettes, aim for 5-8 large flat shapes, at most 3 muted foreground colors and at least one third empty transparent space. Recognizable at 160x90 and clean at 320x180. Optically center the complete main motif in the full canvas with balanced transparent margins; do not reserve an empty text column. Use off-center placement only when necessary for the specific meaning, interaction or direction of action. Centering does not require mirrored or rigidly symmetric objects. At most one flat shadow plane; no realistic lighting, reflections, grain, fine textures, tiny repeated details, decorative scenery, 3D or photorealism. Preserve factual identity and avoid visible contradictions, but leave qualifications and explanations to the article. Default to no text; never add a caption merely naming the pictured object. No legends, axes, connectors or numerical readouts just for completeness. Restrained grown-up magazine artwork. Genuinely transparent background: no backdrop rectangle, black or near-black fill, dark gradient, vignette, decorative glow, border or edge color. Empty areas and corners must be transparent so the card shows through. Preserve alpha. If transparency is technically impossible, use only the supplied exact uniform fallback color. Soft translucent forms are allowed when the selected subject is light or mist, never as a backdrop.
